summary: Frontend-only testing of Brand Studio customization (banner, studio title, 15 accent colors, 3 typography packs with premium gating) and app-wide emoji removal, on Expo web preview (mobile viewport 375x667), coach jcgfit@gmail.com (premium) + 3 fresh throwaway coach signups (non-premium). CONFIRMED WORKING: banner upload/preview/removal (reflects on CoachHome header behind banner), Studio Title override + fallback to auto-generated title when cleared, 15 accent swatches render (7 free + 8 premium-locked with lock icons for non-premium accounts), 3 typography rows render in visually distinct fonts (Signature/Oswald, Bold Impact/Anton, Editorial Mono/SpaceMono) with correct premium lock icons for non-premium accounts, backend PUT /api/me/theme and /api/me/brand both persist correctly (verified via network capture + full page reload showing correct saved state), emoji removal confirmed clean on Home, role-select, onboarding, Programs tab (category badges use icons not emoji), Settings specialty chips (plain text, no emoji), Booking page. FOUND ONE CRITICAL BUG (see below) that undermines the whole live-preview promise of the feature: selecting any accent color or font pack visually SNAPS BACK to the previous selection within ~1-2s of tapping it, on BOTH premium and non-premium accounts, even though the underlying PUT request succeeds and the choice IS correctly persisted server-side (confirmed only visible again after a full page reload). This makes the feature look completely broken to a real user despite the backend being correct.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: Picking a new accent color or font pack in Brand Studio visually reverts to the OLD selection within ~1-2 seconds, even though the PUT /api/me/theme call succeeds (200) and the new value IS saved correctly server-side. Root cause: the useEffect that syncs theme from `user` has `accentColor`/`fontPack` themselves in its OWN dependency array. Flow: pickAccent() -> setAccent(a) optimistically calls setAccentColor(a.brand) (local state) + fires PUT in background (no refreshUser() afterwards). This state change re-triggers the useEffect (because accentColor is a dependency), which re-reads `user?.theme_color` from AuthContext -- but AuthContext's `user` object was NEVER refreshed with the new value (setAccent/setFontPack never call refreshUser()), so `user.theme_color` is still the OLD value. The effect sees `accent.brand !== accentColor` (true, since accentColor just changed to the NEW value) and immediately calls applyAccent(oldAccent) + setAccentColor(oldValue) again, undoing the user's tap. Verified via network capture: PUT payload confirmed correct new color sent + 200 response, but same-session UI reverts; a hard page reload afterwards correctly shows the new color selected (proving persistence works, only the live client-side sync is broken).

Every accent color or font pack change increments ThemeContext's `version` state, which is used as a `key` prop on the single View wrapping the ENTIRE app Stack navigator. This forces a full unmount/remount of every screen in the navigation stack on every single theme tweak (not just a style recalculation), causing visible flicker and resetting scroll position to the top of whatever screen is showing (reproduced consistently on Brand Studio: scrolling down to the color/typography section and tapping a swatch always snaps the ScrollView back to the top). This is a very heavy-handed way to force color/font re-render and compounds the revert bug above by making it hard for users to even see what they tapped.

Could not visually confirm the 'Premium color... upgrade' Alert.alert() actually renders on Web when a non-premium account taps a locked swatch (e.g. Onyx Gold) — no browser-native dialog event fired (Playwright 'dialog' listener never triggered) and no custom on-screen modal was visible in screenshots taken immediately after the tap. This may be a side-effect of the scroll-reset bug above masking the alert, or Alert.alert() may not be wired for react-native-web in this app. Needs manual verification on a native device or with RN Web's Alert polyfill checked directly.

action_items: Fix ThemeContext.tsx useEffect: remove `accentColor`/`fontPack` from its own dependency array (or better, call `refreshUser()` inside setAccent()/setFontPack() right after the PUT succeeds, and let AuthContext's user update naturally drive the effect instead of relying on the effect's self-referential deps). This is the CRITICAL fix — without it, users will believe color/font selection is broken since their tap visibly reverts.

Reconsider the `key={version}` full-Stack remount in app/_layout.tsx — a full app remount on every theme tweak is excessive; the underlying `colors`/`fonts` are already mutated module-level objects, so a lighter-weight re-render mechanism (e.g. a context version number consumed only by StyleSheet-dependent leaf components, or forcing a re-render via context value change without remounting the whole Stack) would avoid the scroll-reset/flicker side effect.

Verify Alert.alert() for locked premium colors/fonts actually surfaces on web (react-native-web) — could not confirm visually in this environment; recommend a native device check or explicit RN-web Alert polyfill review.
Once the above is fixed, retest the full live-preview flow (color changes should visibly apply within the same tap, no revert, no scroll jump).
critical_code_review_comments: ThemeContext.tsx: the sync useEffect subscribes to the very state variables it also sets inside itself (`accentColor`, `fontPack` in deps AND setAccentColor/setFontPackState in body) — this pattern is fragile and is the direct cause of the critical revert bug found. Prefer deriving from `user` object identity/version only, not from the local mirrored state.

app/_layout.tsx: `<View key={version}>` wrapping the entire <Stack> is a very costly way to force theme re-application; a full app remount has broader risk (loses any in-flight navigation/form state anywhere in the app, not just Brand Studio) whenever the user changes their theme.
branding.py / ThemeContext.tsx ACCENTS+FONT_PACKS catalogs are correctly mirrored (15 colors, 3 font packs, same premium flags) — good separation of server-side enforcement, this part is solid.

success_rate.frontend: 70% — banner/title/lock-gating/emoji-removal all pass; the core 'live preview updates instantly' promise of the color/typography picker fails due to the critical revert bug (functionality persists correctly server-side but the UX is broken)

seed_data_creation: Created 3 throwaway coach accounts (TEST_newcoach<random>@example.com / TestPass1234!) via the app's real sign-up flow to verify non-premium lock behavior; left in DB, low-risk test clutter, easily identifiable by TEST_ prefix and 0 clients/programs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The banner, studio title, 15-color catalog, typography catalog, and server-side premium enforcement are ALL correct and working (confirmed via network capture + DB persistence via reload). The one blocking issue is purely client-side state-sync in ThemeContext.tsx: after fixing the useEffect dependency loop (and ideally calling refreshUser() after theme PUTs), retest that tapping a color/font pack updates the checkmark AND the live preview chip color INSTANTLY and STAYS, without needing a page reload, and without the ScrollView jumping to the top.
rca_of_issue: ThemeContext.tsx ThemeProvider: `useEffect(() => {...}, [user?.theme_color, user?.font_pack, accentColor, fontPack])` includes its own managed state (accentColor, fontPack) in the dependency array. setAccent()/setFontPack() optimistically update accentColor/fontPack via setState, then fire a background PUT to /me/theme WITHOUT calling refreshUser() afterwards. The state update immediately re-fires the useEffect (due to accentColor/fontPack being deps); the effect compares the just-changed local state against the STILL-STALE `user.theme_color`/`user.font_pack` (never refreshed) and, finding a mismatch, forcibly resets accentColor/fontPack back to the old server-known value, incrementing `version` again in the process. Net effect: the user's tap visually reverts almost instantly, though the original PUT call itself already succeeded and persisted correctly (confirmed via a hard page reload afterwards, which re-fetches `user` fresh from the server with the correct new theme_color and displays it correctly, no revert). Reproduced consistently across 1 premium account and 3 fresh non-premium accounts.
